objective: Provide a master document and browser-first add-on package that lets another coding agent continue ResonantOS work with preserved Hot Rod Rig context and deterministic verification gates.

artifacts.purpose: Registers the handoff kit in the Add-on SDK catalog.
Self-contained instructions for another coding agent.
Skill-level workflow for preparing and auditing agent handoffs.
Structured source map, implementation targets, rules, and checks.
Read-only Chrome extension workspace for the handoff package.
Review note for a future Hot Rod Rig task ingestion and execution-control interface.
Self-contained visual mockup of the proposed Hot Rod Rig task control workspace.

sourceEvidence.summary: Main Hot Rod Rig and Z-Rig specification history, including v5.3, v5.5.3, v5.6-v5.9, PANEL-TRUTH, and Micro/Standard/Full modes.
ResonantOS-specific planning and corrections that some prior rig runs were manual or ad hoc rather than full protocol executions.
Checkpoint and status records for v5.6-v5.9 and PANEL-TRUTH test evidence.
Zaphod/Z-Rig project-specific runs and transfer lessons.
Zaphod protocol, role packets, output contract, wave structure, failure routing, and role packet library.
Unified v5.5.3 production specification with tiered modes, gates, mechanisms, and formal contracts.
Execution honesty constraint system with ledger, claim scanner, disclosure footer, and test-count evidence.
Historical v5.5.3/v0.4.0 report and CLI/package notes, with caution to check current run evidence.

operatingRules: Do not claim autonomous Hot Rod Rig completion without ledger or tool evidence.
Use repository AGENTS.md and deterministic tests for coding work.
Keep this add-on read-only except for reviewed intake boundaries.
Do not grant shell, provider, wallet, external-send, external-schedule, or trusted memory-write authority.
Report failed or skipped checks plainly.
completionChecklist: Manifest is listed in index.json and dev-index.json.
Add-ons workspace opens the agent-handoff workspace.
Workspace renders source evidence, rules, package files, and verification gates.
Browser-first tests cover the card and open action.
Build and tests have been run or explicitly reported as not run.
